title: 「be up to no good」表示「在搞鬼／圖謀不軌」
titleZh: 「be up to no good」表示「在搞鬼／圖謀不軌」

source.file: Sentence Structure 200 -「be up to no good」表示「在搞鬼／圖謀不軌」.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.

formula: Subject + be + up to no good

formulas.formula: Subject + be + up to no good
Subject + modal + be + up to no good
Subject + have / has been + up to no good

example: Those kids are being unusually quiet. They are probably up to no good.
exampleZh: 那些孩子安靜得反常。他們大概又在搞鬼了。

examples.en: Those kids are being unusually quiet. They are probably up to no good.
examples.zh: 那些孩子安靜得反常。他們大概又在搞鬼了。
examples.highlight: Those kids are being unusually quiet. They are probably up to no good.

meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：Subject + be + up to no good。

rules.zh: 必須使用正確的 be 動詞 根據主語和時態選擇：
rules.en: Use the correct form of be for the subject and tense: I am up to no good. He is up to no good. They are up to no good. She was up to no good. We were up to no good.
examples: I am up to no good.
He is up to no good.
They are up to no good.
She was up to no good.
We were up to no good.

rules.zh: 這個表達通常不指出確實做了甚麼 Be up to no good 表示某人正在做、策劃或企圖做一些： ● 頑皮的事； ● 惹麻煩的事； ● 不誠實的事； ● 不應該做的事。 說話者通常有所懷疑，但未必知道對方確實在做甚麼。
rules.en: The expression normally does not identify the exact activity. Be up to no good suggests that someone is doing, planning or attempting something naughty, troublesome, dishonest or improper. The speaker is suspicious but may not know exactly what the person is doing.

rules.zh: no good 已經帶有負面意思 一般不會說： 這個句子包含雙重否定，容易令人混亂。如要表示對方沒有做壞事，可以直接說： （他沒有做任何不當的事。）
rules.en: No good already carries a negative meaning. Avoid “He is not up to no good”, whose double negative is confusing. To say that someone is not doing anything bad, say: He is not doing anything wrong.
examples: He is not up to no good.
He is not doing anything wrong.

rules.zh: 這是一個較口語化的慣用表達 它常見於： ● 日常對話； ● 故事； ● 非正式訊息； ● 對可疑行為的評論。 在正式報告、投訴或法律文件中，應直接說明具體行為，而不應只說某人 was up to no good。
rules.en: This is an informal idiom common in everyday conversation, stories, informal messages and comments about suspicious behaviour. In a formal report, complaint or legal document, describe the specific conduct instead of merely saying that someone was up to no good.

rules.zh: 可用於人，也可幽默地形容寵物 （那隻狗正在搗蛋。） 這種用法通常帶有輕鬆或幽默的語氣。
rules.en: It can describe people and, humorously, pets: The dog is up to no good. The pet usage is normally light-hearted or humorous.
examples: The dog is up to no good.

benefits.zh: 在不知道確實發生甚麼時表達懷疑 當你看見可疑行為，但沒有足夠資料說明對方正在做甚麼，便可以使用這個句型。 （孩子們突然安靜下來。他們可能正在搞鬼。）
benefits.en: It expresses suspicion when the exact activity is unknown. Use it when you notice suspicious behaviour but lack enough information to say what is happening: The children suddenly became quiet. They may be up to no good.

benefits.zh: 把較長的說法縮短 較長說法： 較自然簡潔的說法： 這個表達能用較少文字傳達相近意思。
benefits.en: It shortens a longer statement. Compare: They appear to be planning or doing something dishonest or troublesome. They appear to be up to no good. The idiom conveys a similar meaning more naturally and concisely.

benefits.zh: 令故事更有懸念 使用 up to no good 時，你不必立即說明人物正在做甚麼，因此可以令讀者產生好奇。 （有人在屋外走動。他看來心懷不軌。）
benefits.en: It creates suspense. Because up to no good does not immediately reveal what a character is doing, it can make readers curious: Someone was moving around outside the house. He seemed to be up to no good.

benefits.zh: 適合表達不同程度的肯定 你可以配合不同字詞，控制語氣： ● may be up to no good：可能在搞鬼； ● probably up to no good：大概在搞鬼； ● clearly up to no good：顯然在搞鬼； ● must be up to no good：一定在搞鬼。
benefits.en: It expresses different degrees of certainty. Use may be up to no good for possibility, probably up to no good for probability, clearly up to no good for an evident judgement, and must be up to no good for a strong deduction.

benefits.zh: 讓日常英語更加自然 英語使用者在談論頑皮、可疑或不誠實的行為時，經常使用這個慣用表達。掌握它有助你理解日 常對話、電影和故事。
benefits.en: It makes everyday English more natural. English speakers often use the idiom when discussing naughty, suspicious or dishonest behaviour, so knowing it also helps you understand everyday conversation, films and stories.
